newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett-Packard stock surges on strong profits.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett-Packard stock surges on strong profits.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co. shares surged in heavy trading Wednesday, a day after the computer and printer maker reported surprisingly strong first-quarter profits that were its highest in eight years.
Morgan Stanley & Co., Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette and Goldman Sachs & Co. upgraded their ratings on H-P's stock and boosted their earnings estimates on the company.
The stock rose $6.50 to $56 on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most active issue at mid-morning.

Late Tuesday, H-P reported profits of $912 million, or 87 cents a share, on revenues of $10.3 billion in its first quarter ended Jan. 31. In the year-ago period, it earned $790 million, or 75 cents a share, on revenues of $9.3 billion.
Analysts had expected earnings per share to be unchanged.

"Nearly all of the positive earnings surprise was driven by improved gross margins," NatWest Securities said in a report. It said the company's gross profit margin rose to 35 percent from 32.8 percent in the fourth quarter.
Natwest continued to recommend accumulating H-P stock, which it said was "very attractive" at current levels and could reach $66 in 12 months.
NatWest raised its earnings estimate for 1997 and 1988.
